title: Bangsamoro uncovers scholarship corruption, teacher posts for sale, unused computers, salaries for the dead
summary: An audit done by BARMM's Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education uncovers systemic corruption, payroll discrepancies, damaged supplies, and hiring scandals

blocks.text: INSPECTION. Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education chief Naguib Sinarimbo conducts a surprise visit and inspection of warehouses in Cotabato City on November 19, 2026, to assess the status of the supplies they have for the region.
An audit done by BARMM's Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education uncovers systemic corruption, payroll discrepancies, damaged supplies, and hiring scandals

COTABATO CITY, Philippines – A team led by Minister Naguib Sinarimbo on Thursday, November 19, uncovered signs of possible systemic corruption during a surprise inspection of warehouses of the Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education (MBHTE).

The rapid internal audit of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) education agency also found deep-seated administrative breakdowns, unutilized supplies, and alleged corruption schemes that ranged from tampered scholarship accounts to cash-for-item bribery in the hiring of teachers.

Sinarimbo said an immediate step they will take is ton overhaul the administrative and payroll systems within the ministry. MBHTE will also engage with the Bangsamoro Parliament for new policies or legislation need to introduce the necessary reforms.

Meanwhile, he acknowledged that, while issues about the quality of education will not be solved overnight, reform can begin with the proper recruitment and deployment of teachers where they are most needed.
He called on all sectors to unite in fixing the region’s education sector.
Below are the anomalies uncovered during the inspections and internal audit, and the immediate ways Minister Sinarimbo directed the MBHTE to take.

blocks.caption: UNUSABLE. Nearly 2,000 tablets were found stored, and unusable, in a warehouse of the Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education in Cotabato during a surprise  inspection on November 19, 2026. Ferdinandh Cabrera/Rappler

items: They were sitting idle and already non-functional in ministry warehouses in Cotabato City.
They were delivered in 2022, but returned or stored away because they no longer worked.
Other computer sets delivered in 2023 were also found in the warehouses.
Solution: Check if guarantees are still available.

blocks.text: Damaged books and other teaching materials

items: The materials included teacher and learner kits, sports equipment, and materials for Indigenous Peoples Education and Madrasah or ISAL teachers.
They were found dusty, moldy, or damaged.
Some dated back to the era of the former Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (ARMM) before 2019.
Solution: Move the inventory, first in materials are first to be disposed or pulled out.
Allowances of some scholars had not been released for months.
The allowances of several students were deposited in a common account under another individual’s name.
Ministry personnel were involved in the scheme.
Solution: A formal investigation into the scheme has been launched, with a participant already agreeing to cooperate.
Applicants for teaching positions were asked to pay between ₱100,000 and ₱300,000 to get the items.
Some who had already made advance payments still didn’t get the positions promised to them.
Insiders were involved, Schools Division superintendents told the Minister.
Solution: The MBHTE will open a hotline for tips and complaints.
Solution: Sinarimbo said the cases will go through due process and be filed with the Bangsamoro Attorney General’s Office or the Office of the Ombudsman.
Schools Division Offices reported mismatches in payroll records and actual head counts. It was identified as the biggest lingering administrative problem.

Long delays in updating of teachers’ records resulted in: Retired or deceased teachers still receiving salaries. It took six months to one year to remove them from the payroll, so they still got ₱400,000 to ₱600,000 in excess wages. Bereaved families unable to collect benefits until the overpayments are settled.
When teachers are promoted, the contributions deducted from their salaries remain tied to their old, lower pay.
This resulted in loan problems and ballooning unpaid balances.
Penalties for the discrepancies surface only near the teachers’ retirement.
